title: Fact-Check Grounding Loss for Semantically Consistent Model Editing

contributions.purpose: Close the semantic-consistency gap where edited models cannot reliably judge the truth of statements containing their own edited facts.
contributions.mechanism: Fact-Check Grounding (FCG) augments the standard editing objective with balanced truth-conditional supervision, training the model to judge the new fact as True (FC-Pos) and the old fact as False (FC-Neg) via an auxiliary loss (weight lambda=0.3), preventing an 'always True' shortcut.
contributions.evaluation: Method-level; format-only control (unbalanced) achieves only chance-level 50% BFC-Acc, motivating the balanced design.
contributions.domain: Knowledge / model editing of LLM factual associations
contributions.source_quote: We propose FCG, a method that augments model editing with balanced True/False supervision to improve semantic consistency.

contributions.purpose: Quantify FCG's improvement in balanced fact-check accuracy over a baseline.
contributions.mechanism: Compare FCG against LocFT-BF baseline and a format-only control on the KnowEdit ZsRE benchmark with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
contributions.evaluation: FCG improves balanced fact-check accuracy (BFC-Acc) by +12.3 points over LocFT-BF (58.06% vs 45.77%, p=0.0044), while format-only training achieves only chance-level performance (50%).
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that FCG improves balanced fact-check accuracy (BFC-Acc) by +12.3 points over the LocFT-BF baseline (p=0.0044) on KnowEdit ZsRE, while the format-only control achieves only chance-level performance.

contributions.purpose: Disclose the boundary of FCG's effectiveness.
contributions.mechanism: Test transfer of the fact-check improvement to paraphrased prompts.
contributions.evaluation: Important limitation: improvement is template-specific with limited paraphrase transfer (+2.44 points, not statistically significant), indicating FCG learns template-label associations rather than semantically robust truth-judgment.
contributions.domain: Generalization / robustness analysis of model editing
contributions.source_quote: We reveal an important limitation: FCG's improvement is template-specific, with limited transfer to paraphrased prompts (+2.44 points, not significant), indicating that the model learns template-label associations rather than semantically robust truth-judgment.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Methods such as ROME (Meng et al. 2022a), MEMIT (Meng et al. 2022b), and localized fine-tuning (Yang et al. 2025b) have demonstrated success in modifying model outputs for targeted prompts while preserving general capabilities. However, current editing methods focus primarily on token-level generation accuracy...
Recent work has revealed a critical gap: edited models often cannot reliably judge the truth of statements containing their own edited facts (Liu et al., 2025).
We propose Fact-Check Grounding (FCG), which augments the standard editing objective with balanced truth-conditional supervision.

notes: Limitation/partial-negative result flagged by the paper itself: FCG's gains do NOT transfer to paraphrased prompts (+2.44 points, not statistically significant), interpreted as learning template-label associations rather than robust truth-judgment.
